title: Phrasal verbs 9: away/back
subtitle: drive away / give back
summary: Learn phrasal verbs with away (moving or going from a place) and back (returning, or doing the same thing in return).

lesson.heading: away or back?

left.label: away = away from home or from a place
examples: Sarah got into her car, started the engine and **drove away**.
I tried to take a picture of the bird, but it **flew away**.
The police searched the house and **took away** a computer.

right.label: back = back home or back to a place
examples: *A:* I'm going out now. *B:* What time will you be **back**?
After eating at a restaurant, we **walked back** to our hotel.
I've still got Jane's keys. I forgot to **give them back** to her.

lesson.note: In the same way you can say walk away, run away, look away ... and go back, come back, get back, take something back.

lesson.heading: get away, get away with, keep away
lesson.text: **get away** = escape, leave with difficulty. **get away with something** = do something wrong without being caught. **keep away (from ...)** = don't go near.

examples.text: We tried to catch the thief, but she **got away**.
I parked in a no-parking zone, but I **got away with it**. I didn't have to pay a fine.
**Keep away** from the edge of the pool. You might fall in.

lesson.heading: give away, put away, throw away
lesson.text: **give something away** = give it to somebody because you don't want it any more. **put something away** = put it in the place where it is usually kept. **throw something away** = put it in the rubbish.

examples.text: *A:* Did you sell your bike? *B:* No, I **gave it away** to a friend.
When the children finished playing with their toys, they **put them away**.
I kept the letter, but I **threw away** the envelope.

lesson.heading: wave back, smile back
lesson.text: **back** can also mean doing the same thing in return: **wave back**, **smile back**, **shout back**, **hit somebody back**.

examples.text: I waved to her, and she **waved back**.
He wasn't very friendly. I smiled at him, but he didn't **smile back**.

lesson.heading: call back, get back to, look back, pay back
lesson.text: **call/phone/ring (somebody) back** = return a phone call. **get back to somebody** = reply to them. **look back (on something)** = think about what happened in the past. **pay back** money, **pay somebody back** = return money you borrowed.

examples.text: I can't talk to you now. I'll **call you back** in ten minutes.
I sent him an email, but he never **got back to** me.
My first job was in a travel agency. I didn't like it much at the time but, **looking back on it**, I learnt a lot.
If you borrow money, you have to **pay it back**.
Thanks for lending me the money. I'll **pay you back** next week.

lesson.text: Careful with *give away* and *give back*: you give something away to somebody who can keep it, but you give something back to its owner.

exercises.prompt: She waved to him and he ___.
exercises.explanation: back can mean doing the same thing in return: he waved back.

exercises.prompt: It was windy. I dropped a twenty-pound note and it ___.
exercises.explanation: blow away = be carried away by the wind.

exercises.prompt: She opened the letter, read it and ___ in the envelope.
exercises.explanation: put something back = return it to where it was.

exercises.prompt: His shoes were worn out, so he ___.
exercises.explanation: throw something away = put it in the rubbish.

exercises.prompt: I saw a man trying to break into a car. When he saw me, he ___.
exercises.explanation: run away = leave quickly to escape.

exercises.prompt: Be careful! That's an electric fence. Make sure you ___ from it.
exercises.explanation: keep away from something = don't go near it.

exercises.prompt: Jane doesn't do anything at work. I don't know how she ___ with it.
exercises.explanation: get away with something = do something wrong without being caught.

exercises.prompt: *A:* What happened to all the books you used to have? *B:* I didn't want them any more, so I ___.
exercises.explanation: give something away = give it to somebody because you don't want it.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Here's the money you asked me to lend you. *B:* Thanks. I'll ___ as soon as I can.
exercises.explanation: pay somebody back = return the money you borrowed from them.

exercises.statement: I sent him an email, but he never got back to me.
exercises.explanation: Correct. get back to somebody = reply to them.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrasal verb with its meaning.

pairs.right: do something wrong without being caught
put it where it is usually kept
think about what happened in the past

exercises.prompt: Does each sentence need away or back?

items.text: Sarah got into her car and drove ...
I forgot to give Jane's keys ... to her.
I tried to photograph the bird, but it flew ...
After the meal we walked ... to our hotel.
The police searched the house and took ... a computer.
When you've finished with that book, put it ... on the shelf.
